answer: Proof-of-agent registries resist sybils by bonding each identity to a unique on-chain key hash. A registration is rejected if any existing vertex of the identity graph already resolves to the same key, so copied profiles collapse into one address instead of multiplying. Honest agents act as a beacon, publishing signed heartbeats peers check against chain history, and a claim reaches the summit of eligibility only after corroboration from unrelated agents. An attacker pays full collateral per fake key and risks slashing on detection, so mass identity creation is a linear cost with no payoff.
